history.summary: Identity flag: no 'Jain Glass Temple' in Tonk district or Tonk town could be verified anywhere online after targeted searching - the well-documented Jain Glass Temple is the one in NAGAUR city (behind Kamla Tower / near Oswal Bhavan, Khas Bazar, General Ganj), so the CSV town 'Tonk' and district 'Tonk' appear to be a row-level error; file documents the Nagaur temple as the best-supported referent (verify with the master CSV). The Nagaur Jain Glass Temple, also called Shri Digambar Jain Atishaya Kshetra Mandir or Shri Mahaveer Swami Jain Mandir, is a Jain shrine famous for glass-and-mirror mosaic work covering walls, ceilings, pillars, doors and windows; the glasswork depicts scenes from Jain mythology, symbolising the purity and clarity of the soul. It has a white-marble idol of Mahavira (one source names Parsvanath as the presiding deity - verify), a dome-shaped lotus-motif roof with a shikhara, glass chandeliers and a fountain tank. Blends Rajput and Mughal architectural styles. No reliable photograph of this temple could be found online, so media is intentionally empty.
